messages:
alex.t: Heads-up — client POC: logs show ingestion but traces don't link to spans after we enabled the log-drain. Can we triage?
jin: Are trace headers (traceparent / tracestate / x-request-id) making it through their proxy?
rowan: Their nginx was configured to drop unknown headers by default. I saw that in the env we deployed.
infra-bot: Incident 6023 created: "POC trace-log correlation missing" — assignees: jin, rowan.
jin: Quick test: curl a sample event to the forwarder including traceparent and see it in Datadog. Example: `curl -X POST https://forwarder.example.com/ingest -H "traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01" -d '{"msg":"test","trace_id":"abc"}'`
rowan: Also check forwarder logs for 429/backoff — we recently saw short bursts drop during heavy batching.
amy_sales: Customer worried about timeline; if we can't get this working with Datadog can we ship to Splunk instead?
jin: Splunk HEC works but field mappings differ (we send `trace.id`). Easiest fix: 1) enable header passthrough on nginx, 2) confirm token scopes include trace-linking, 3) temporarily enable forwarder debug to catch 429s.
alex.t: Can infra do remote nginx change or do they require a redeploy?
rowan: We can patch nginx via their bastion (no redeploy) but need a maintenance window and firewall allowlist (we'll share IPs).
jin: I'll attach a short runbook and a dashboard snippet to detect gaps (trace_count vs log_ingest). amy_sales: I'll tell the client we have a plan and ETA EOD.
